match.reason: The bank point covers insulin, glucagon and negative feedback well, but it never mentions type 1 diabetes, which the new point requires, so adding that idea would be more than a small change.

draft.title: Regulating blood glucose
card: Cells use glucose from the blood to release energy. Blood glucose must stay within a narrow range, so hormones adjust it. The pancreas detects the level and releases the hormones.
released when blood glucose is high, such as after a meal. It causes cells to take up glucose from the blood, and the liver to store it as glycogen. Blood glucose falls.
released when blood glucose is low, such as between meals. It causes the liver to break down glycogen and release glucose into the blood. Blood glucose rises.
In type 1 diabetes, the body cannot make insulin. Cells cannot take up glucose properly, so blood glucose stays high.
draft.remember: Insulin lowers blood glucose, glucagon raises it, and without insulin blood glucose stays high.

a.q: Ravi has just eaten a large meal and his blood glucose rises. What does his pancreas do in response?
opts: Releases insulin, so blood glucose falls
Releases glucagon, so blood glucose falls
Releases insulin, so blood glucose rises
Releases glucagon, so blood glucose rises
a.why: A high blood glucose level triggers the release of insulin, which moves glucose into cells and into storage as glycogen. Glucagon is the tempting wrong choice, but it is released when blood glucose is low and it raises the level.
a.clue: Which hormone is released when blood glucose is high?

b.q: Mia has type 1 diabetes and has not taken any insulin. She eats a meal. Why does her blood glucose stay high?
opts: Her cells cannot take up glucose without insulin
Her liver releases too much glycogen without glucagon
Her pancreas makes too much insulin after the meal
Her cells cannot use glucagon to take up glucose
b.why: Type 1 diabetes means the body cannot make insulin, so glucose is not taken up by cells or stored by the liver, and it stays in the blood. Glucagon is not the problem: it raises blood glucose and does not move glucose into cells.
b.clue: Which hormone is missing in type 1 diabetes, and what does it do to glucose in cells?

a.best: Releases insulin, so blood glucose falls

b.best: Her cells cannot take up glucose without insulin

problems.detail: The right option says cells 'cannot take up glucose without insulin', which is more absolute than the card's 'cannot take up glucose properly'. Some cells, such as brain cells, take up glucose without insulin. Matching the card, for example 'cannot take up glucose properly without insulin', would avoid overstating it.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate and the answers are clear. The only issue is minor: question b's right option drops the card's 'properly' and so overstates that cells cannot take up any glucose without insulin.
